svg.aria-label: Flower Anatomy Drag and Drop interactive study plate
svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop — Plate 07
svg.desc: A static SVG learning interface. Ten label tiles in a word bank can be selected to fill ten label slots around a cutaway flower diagram. Hint, Check Answer and Reset open popups. No JavaScript.

g.text: PLATE 07 · ANGIOSPERM MORPHOLOGY · INTERACTIVE STUDY SHEET
DIAGRAM · LONGITUDINAL SECTION OF A TYPICAL FLOWER
Fig. 1 — the four whorls: sepals, petals, stamens and carpels, seated on the receptacle.
Terminology follows standard floral morphology — the male whorl (androecium) is anther plus filament;
the female whorl (gynoecium) is stigma, style and ovary, all seated on the receptacle.
Pick a tile from the word bank below.
Ten terms · ten empty slots on the plate.
Drop it on the slot beside its structure.
The leader line shows exactly where it belongs.
Press Check Answer to review the key.
Score one point per correct placement.
SELECT A TILE TO PLACE IT · SELECT IT AGAIN TO RETURN IT TO THE BANK
Plate 07 · drawn for classroom use · terms follow Harris & Harris, Plant Identification Terminology
Static SVG · no scripts · state driven by CSS targets and selectors
Petals attract pollinators with colour and scent.
Sepals protect the bud and sit outermost.
Look for them lowest on the flower, at the base.
The anther is the pollen-bearing sac at the tip.
The filament is the slender stalk that holds it up.
Stigma: sticky landing pad for pollen.
Style: the tube the pollen grows down.
Ovary: houses the ovules; ripens into fruit.
The thickened stem tip that holds every whorl.
It sits directly beneath the ovary, where the
flower joins the pedicel (the flower stalk).
Memory line — sepals, petals, stamens, carpels: from the outside in.
TEN TERMS · TEN SLOTS · ONE POINT EACH
showy inner whorl, left and right of the section
green leaf-like base, outermost, lowest pair
whole male part: anther carried on a filament
whole female part: stigma, style and ovary
gold pollen sac at the tip of each filament
the column joining stigma to ovary
receptive tip; receives the pollen grain
the base that holds all the whorls
9–10 correct: excellent · 6–8: revisit the whorls · under 6: open the Hint panel and rebuild the flower from the base up.
Every tile you placed is still reversible — nothing on this plate is permanent.
Select any placed tile in the word bank
the term returns to the bank and its slot goes dashed again
receptacle, ovary, style, stigma — then the stamens, then the perianth
see how quickly you can name all ten structures
Tip for teachers: project this plate, hide the word bank with a sheet of paper,
and ask students to name each structure aloud before they place the tiles.
